objective: Raise expected facade construction/material/period fidelity by replacing the known low-fidelity pair of rubber-looking window handle blocks with a period-plausible mechanically assembled metal crescent latch and receiver, while preserving fail-closed native-4K evidence discipline.

decision.whyThisTask: The existing sliding-window metadata explicitly described HD_WindowHandle_* as fallback dark hardware using the EPDM/rubber palette. That is a high-value close-crop material/construction mismatch: a circa-2000 Japanese two-panel sliding sash should read as mechanically fastened lock hardware, not two rubber bars. Correcting this improves a repeatedly visible hero interface and reduces future impossible-material/period-authenticity deductions more directly than adding another provenance-only guard.
researchBasis: LIXIL sliding-window parts taxonomy separates crescent lock, crescent receiver and pull handle as distinct components.

LIXIL/Tostem AAAZC07L is documented as a metal crescent lock with 50 mm mounting-screw pitch and compatibility including Atmos II from 1996-10 and Thermal II/PG from 1999-02, directly supporting a circa-2000 part class and pitch.

Older LIXIL/Tostem metal crescent replacements also document mechanically fastened lock construction with different pitches; therefore only the 50 mm pitch and general part class are treated as period-supported here. Other dimensions remain explicit reconstruction assumptions.

lod0Components: 30 x combined six-segment crescent lever mesh
implementation.geometryPolicy: No Unity stock Cube/Cylinder/Plane/Quad is used as finished latch geometry. Metric-UV clones of the existing authored detail mesh library are cached under GeneratedFacadeHardwareMeshes/SashLatch. Eight deterministic physical-UV phases at 11 mm spacing reduce synchronized microresponse across thirty windows.
implementation.materialPolicy: Primary latch/receiver uses canonical aged sash aluminum; screws use canonical dark galvanized hardware. Both are physically metallic Standard materials, dry in the benchmark, non-emissive, and reflection-driven rather than carrying painted highlights.
implementation.weatheringPolicy: LOD0 body/pivot/receiver are sheltered+recessed with low rain, mild UV/recess grime and increased contact only on the operating lever. Fasteners add a localized ferrous-fixture source. No arbitrary damage or source-free rust is introduced.
implementation.lodPolicy: Thirty independent per-window four-level LODGroups use animated cross-fade. Close LOD0 preserves lock construction; LOD1/2/3 progressively remove sub-pixel fastener/pivot complexity while retaining hardware silhouette before culling.
implementation.formalEvidencePolicy: The reflection-material fingerprint now requires the latch contract, may build a genuinely missing latch pass only on the first pre-probe evaluation, freezes the generated root instance ID, and fails closed if the root is removed/replaced or legacy rubber handles are re-enabled during later reflection polls. MainCamera native-4K pre-cull independently validates the same state.

specificPixelRisks: The reconstructed 30 x 82 mm plate and 34 mm crescent radius may read too large/small against the generated meeting stiles despite source-side plausibility.
The six-segment crescent may facet visibly in a 100% 4K crop and require a true curved extrusion after rendered review.
Small metallic hardware may sparkle or alias under grazing midsummer sun if mip/AA/LOD behavior is insufficient.
Latch/receiver may intersect the meeting-stile or gasket depth stack because Unity runtime scene serialization has not been inspected.

The global material/construction registry still describes the disabled legacy HD_WindowHandle_* fallback; active latch construction is instead governed by the new dedicated contract and Danchi-domain metadata. Runtime metadata coverage validation must confirm no critical gap before scoring.
